verdicts.title: Per-group clipping crashes DDP training on any partially-empty Poisson round
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced end to end. Single-process check with clipped_grad(clipping_norm=PerGroup(...), return_aux=True): a batch of 4 yields aux.clipping_rate=None (because _compute_clipping_stats returns a per-group dict at _clipped_fun.py:499-510 and the ClippedFunAux/ClippedGradAux constructor at _clipped_fun.py:849-856 collapses any non-float, non-None rate to None), while a batch of 0 takes the short-circuit at _clipped_grad.py:238 and yields aux.clipping_rate=0.0. Ran a real 2-rank gloo spawn: rank 0 empty -> 0.0, rank 1 bs=4 -> None, and _sync_clipping_rate's presence check (_distributed.py:224-230) raised 'Clipped auxiliary clipping_rate presence mismatch across ranks.' on BOTH ranks; a subsequent all_reduce/barrier still succeeded, so it is fail-closed, not a hang or silent desync. Reachability verified in the trainer: _dp_trainer.py:1405-1421 builds a PerGroup clip_norm from the documented TrainingArguments.clipping_norm dict, :4176-4185 passes it to clipped_grad(return_aux=True), :2102-2104 calls opaque sync(clip_state, aux) under DDP. The adaptive path has the same divergence (_adaptive.py:423 hardcodes clipping_rate=0.0 on the empty branch vs :617 propagating aux.clipping_rate which is None under PerGroup). The shipped regression helper _worker_sync_aux_empty_vs_per_group (packages/opaque-engine/tests/ddp/engine_ddp_helpers.py:672-715) hand-builds the non-empty rank with clipping_rate=0.5, a float that real per-group clipped_grad never emits, so it passes while the real path crashes. Not epsilon-affecting (fail-closed abort). Severity medium rather than high: it requires per-group clipping + DDP + an empty Poisson draw on some-but-not-all ranks, and it aborts loudly rather than corrupting the mechanism. No open tracked issue covers it (#368 is the closed fix that introduced the presence check).
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: DPTrainer with a per-group TrainingArguments.clipping_norm dict (clipping_mode 'fixed' or 'adaptive') under DDP with Poisson sampling. On any step where at least one rank draws an empty batch and at least one does not, the empty rank reports clipping_rate=0.0 while every non-empty rank reports None (per-group rates are a dict and are collapsed to None by the aux constructor). _sync_clipping_rate's min/max presence collective then disagrees and raises RuntimeError('Clipped auxiliary clipping_rate presence mismatch across ranks.') on every rank, aborting the run mid-training. Verified live on 2-rank gloo; the process group is left usable (follow-up collectives succeed), so this is a fail-closed crash, not silent corruption or a hang.

verdicts.title: Distributed CI lane passes silently if its test selection collapses to zero
verdicts.reasoning: Every link verified by reading the workflows. .github/workflows/pr.yml:76-85 and ci.yml:41-50 both call python-tests.yml with allow-empty-test-selection: true and pytest-marker 'distributed and not cuda'. python-tests.yml:91 forwards it as ALLOW_EMPTY_TEST_SELECTION, and .github/scripts/run_python_test_package.sh:40-43 converts pytest exit 5 into exit 0 with only a ::notice::. The job's 'Run test group' step (python-tests.yml:110-122) only ORs the per-path exit codes, so if all five matrix suites collect nothing the whole lane is green with zero tests run. TEST_RESULTS_FILE is written by the script but grep over .github/ shows it is never read by any step or workflow -- it is a dead variable, confirming there is no non-emptiness assertion. Note this is a latent, not active, hole: I collected 9 distributed tests today (uv run pytest packages/opaque-engine -m 'distributed and not cuda' --collect-only -> 9 collected), so the lane currently does execute work. The failure requires a future marker rename, conftest deselection, or test relocation. Severity low: no user-visible defect, purely a CI guardrail gap. Broad open CI issues (#325 packaging/supply-chain CI, #429, #666) do not cover this fail-open, so already_tracked is 0.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: Latent CI fail-open, not an active one. Today the distributed lane collects 9 tests. If a future change renames the 'distributed' marker, deselects the ddp directories via conftest, or moves the spawn tests outside packages/*/tests and tests/, every one of the five matrix suites exits with pytest code 5; run_python_test_package.sh:40-43 turns that into exit 0 under allow-empty-test-selection: true, the job's failed flag stays 0, and the branch-protection gate reports success with zero distributed tests executed. Nothing in python-tests.yml asserts that any suite collected tests (TEST_RESULTS_FILE is written but never read anywhere in .github/), so the collective-desync regression class this lane exists to block could reland unnoticed.

verdicts.title: Optimizer-state drift audit marshals float64 fingerprints through float32 collectives with rtol=1e-5
verdicts.reasoning: Code path verified and reproduced. optimizers/distributed.py:97-102 casts each tensor to double() then hands the four stats to assert_scalar_equal with no compute_dtype; engine/distributed/_state.py:57-70 and :171-181 then marshal the float through a torch.float32 collective tensor and compare with torch.isclose(atol=1e-8, rtol=1e-5) in float32. Ran a 2-rank gloo repro of _assert_tensor_fingerprint_equal: a uniform 1e-6 relative drift on a 1000-element float32 tensor PASSED the audit undetected on both ranks; a 1e-3 relative drift was correctly caught. So the audit does catch gross desync but is blind below ~1e-5 relative, and the double() precision is computed and then discarded. One correction to the reporter's framing: the dominant limitation is the rtol=1e-5 default, not the float32 marshalling -- passing compute_dtype=torch.float64 alone would not detect 1e-6 drift, so a fix must tighten atol/rtol too. Severity low: this is a debug/audit facility, not a mechanism; no privacy or numerical guarantee depends on it, and real desync (identical-key noise + pure-function updates diverging) would normally be far larger than 1e-5. No open issue covers it (#365 was the closed integer-half fix; #321 is closed).
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: Under DDP, sync_optimizer_state fingerprints each optimizer-state tensor in float64 but compares the four statistics through a float32 collective with torch.isclose(atol=1e-8, rtol=1e-5). Verified on 2-rank gloo: a uniform 1e-6 relative difference between two ranks' state tensors passes the audit silently, while 1e-3 is caught. Cross-rank optimizer-state drift below roughly 1e-5 relative therefore goes unreported by an audit whose stated purpose (module docstring, optimizers/distributed.py:85-93) is drift detection; the binding constraint is the rtol default, with float32 marshalling as a secondary ceiling (~1e-7 relative for large sums).

verdicts.title: DPTrainer never consults ScheduleFreeState.x: schedule-free eval and checkpoints use the wrong weight sequence
verdicts.reasoning: Verified by direct grep and reading. _optim.py:55 registers 'schedule_free' and :94 maps HF's 'schedule_free_radam' to it; _build_schedule_free (:165-216) constructs the wrapper and returns it with no warning of any kind. grep for ScheduleFreeState across the repo hits only opaque-optimizers sources/tests plus the facade re-export -- packages/opaque-transformers/src contains zero references, and grep for opt_state/published in _dp_trainer.py finds no consumer of the .x field. The trainer therefore treats the wrapper's params argument (y_t) as the model weights for eval, best-model selection, checkpointing and save. The wrapper's own module docstring (_schedule_free.py:41-48) states this explicitly: 'Saving / evaluating against y_t would defeat the purpose of schedule-free averaging ... This is the dependency that gates schedule-free's usefulness through DPTrainer.' With the paper default beta=0.9 (verified at _schedule_free.py:186), y_t = 0.1*z_t + 0.9*x_t, so the exported model retains 10 percent of the raw noisy iterate against x_t's Var/n. docs/reference/transformers.md:229-234 lists schedule_free among supported optim values with no eval/save caveat. Issue #408 ('Provide the documented schedule-free evaluation accessor') is closed as completed and its parent #321 is closed, but neither covers the trainer-side consumption, and its closing PR #714 was itself closed rather than merged; nothing in the open list tracks this. Severity medium: silent utility degradation of a documented supported option, no privacy or correctness violation (x_t is post-processing of an already-private trajectory).
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A user sets optim='schedule_free' (or the HF alias schedule_free_radam) on DPTrainer. Training is privacy-correct, but no code in opaque-transformers ever reads ScheduleFreeState.x, so every eval metric, best-model selection, checkpoint and final save reflects the forward-pass iterate y_t = (1-beta)z_t + beta*x_t (beta defaults to 0.9, so 10 percent raw noisy iterate) instead of the Polyak-averaged published weights x_t. The advertised ~Var/n noise reduction is silently forfeited and no warning is emitted; docs/reference/transformers.md lists schedule_free as supported with no caveat, while docs/reference/optimizers.md:196-197 instructs library users to read opt_state.x -- an accessor the trainer path never reaches.

verdicts.title: Adafactor module docstring misstates the BC default (says True, actual False) plus two stale/incorrect memory statements
verdicts.reasoning: All three sub-claims checked against the exact lines. (1) _adafactor.py:30-31 reads 'noise_bias_correction=True activates this path; defaults to True so BC is on by default', while the signature at :303 is 'noise_bias_correction: bool = False' and the argument docstring at :335-338 correctly says 'Defaults to False' -- the file contradicts itself, and the module header is the misleading half. (2) :28 says the phi-EMA is subtracted 'with a positive floor', but :238-239 is torch.where(corr_row > 0, corr_row, new_v_row) -- when the correction goes non-positive the code falls back to the UNcorrected EMA, which is materially different from clamping to a small positive floor. (3) :5-7 say rank<2 tensors 'fall back to a scalar second moment' and the helper docstring at :106 repeats 'or scalar', but _init_v_for_leaf:120 returns (torch.zeros_like(leaf),) -- a full per-element second moment for vectors. The code is paper-correct (Shazeer and Stern keep full v for non-matrix tensors); the prose is wrong, and it overstates the memory saving. Docs-only; severity low, no epsilon impact. Nothing in the open issue list covers it (#406 is closed).
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A user reads the opaque.api.optimizers._adafactor module header -- the section that sells the DP noise-variance bias correction -- concludes from lines 30-31 that noise_bias_correction defaults to True, and trains with adafactor() defaults. The actual default is False (:303), so the row/column second-moment EMAs silently retain the +sigma^2 DP noise bias the header claims is removed. Two secondary prose errors compound the confusion: line 28 describes the correction as subtracting the phi-EMA 'with a positive floor' when the implementation (:238-239) instead falls back to the uncorrected EMA via torch.where, and lines 5-7 claim rank<2 tensors use a scalar second moment when _init_v_for_leaf:120 allocates a full per-element tensor, overstating the memory saving.

verdicts.title: Fabricated author list 'Defazio, Yaida, Cutkosky' survives the closed citation-repair sweep (#418 / OPQ-136)
verdicts.reasoning: Verified against the primary source and the repository history. packages/opaque-optimizers/src/opaque/api/optimizers/_schedule_free.py:10 reads 'Defazio, Yaida, Cutkosky, "The Road Less Scheduled", arXiv:2405.15682'. Fetching https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.15682 returns authors Aaron Defazio, Xingyu Alice Yang, Harsh Mehta, Konstantin Mishchenko, Ahmed Khaled, Ashok Cutkosky -- 'Yaida' is not among them (Sho Yaida is an unrelated researcher, likely a corruption of 'Yang'). A repo-wide Grep for 'Yaida' returns exactly one source hit, this line (all other hits are the audit's own checkpoint JSON). git show --stat 1d216fcd (the merged citation-repair commit for #418 / PR #503) touches 53 files including _adagrad.py, _adam.py and _rmsprop.py under opaque-optimizers but never _schedule_free.py, confirming the sweep skipped this site. #418 is closed as completed and its parent #324 is closed; nothing in the open issue list tracks it. Severity low: a source-comment citation error with no runtime effect.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: packages/opaque-optimizers/src/opaque/api/optimizers/_schedule_free.py:10 attributes arXiv:2405.15682 'The Road Less Scheduled' to 'Defazio, Yaida, Cutkosky'. The arXiv record lists Defazio, Yang, Mehta, Mishchenko, Khaled, Cutkosky; 'Yaida' is not an author. A reviewer verifying the schedule-free averaging implementation against its primary source searches on the printed author list, finds Sho Yaida's unrelated work, and either wastes time or propagates the fabricated attribution downstream. This is the sole remaining instance in the tree, and the merged citation-repair commit 1d216fcd for the closed #418 never touched this file.
